questions.stem: Two organisms are classified in the same order but different families. A third organism shares the same class as the first two but is in a different order. Which pair of organisms is most closely related?

options.text: The first and third organisms, because they share more physical features
The first and second organisms, because sharing the same order means they are more closely related than organisms sharing only the same class
The second and third organisms
All three are equally related because they share the same class

questions.explanation: The Linnaean classification hierarchy (from broadest to most specific) is: Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species. Organisms sharing a more specific group (order) are more closely related than those sharing only a broader group (class). The first and second organisms share the same order, making them more closely related than either is to the third.

questions.stem: Carl Woese proposed the three-domain system (Bacteria, Archaea, Eukarya), which replaced the traditional five-kingdom system. What evidence led to this change?

options.text: Microscope observations showed that archaea look different from bacteria
Analysis of ribosomal RNA sequences revealed that archaea are as genetically different from bacteria as they are from eukaryotes
Archaea were discovered to have nuclei, like eukaryotes
Archaea were found to be multicellular organisms

questions.explanation: Woese compared ribosomal RNA sequences across organisms and found that archaea, despite looking superficially similar to bacteria under a microscope, are genetically as different from bacteria as they are from eukaryotes. This molecular evidence justified placing them in a separate domain. Archaea are prokaryotes (no nucleus) like bacteria, but their RNA and cell chemistry are distinct.

questions.stem: Organisms are given a binomial name (e.g., Homo sapiens). What information does the binomial naming system provide, and why is it useful?

options.text: It gives the kingdom and phylum; it is useful for identifying where organisms live
It gives the genus and species; it provides a universal scientific name that avoids confusion caused by different common names in different languages
It gives the family and order; it tells scientists what the organism eats
It gives the class and order; it is only used in English-speaking countries

questions.explanation: Binomial nomenclature uses two Latin names: the genus (capitalised) and species (lowercase), e.g., Homo sapiens. This system, devised by Linnaeus, provides a universal name understood by scientists worldwide, regardless of language. Common names vary between countries and can be ambiguous (e.g., 'robin' refers to different species in the UK and USA).

questions.stem: A new species of deep-sea fish is discovered. Scientists compare its DNA sequence with known fish species. The new fish shares 95% of its DNA with Species X and 80% with Species Y. What can be concluded?

options.text: The new fish is the same species as Species X
The new fish is more closely related to Species X than Species Y, as greater DNA similarity indicates a more recent common ancestor
The new fish is more closely related to Species Y because 80% similarity is more significant
DNA similarity cannot be used to determine evolutionary relationships

questions.explanation: Greater DNA sequence similarity indicates a more recent common ancestor and therefore a closer evolutionary relationship. 95% similarity with Species X means the new fish and Species X diverged more recently than the new fish and Species Y (80%). Molecular phylogenetics uses DNA comparisons to classify organisms and build evolutionary trees.

questions.stem: Traditionally, organisms were classified based on observable physical features. Modern classification increasingly uses DNA analysis. Why might DNA-based classification sometimes disagree with classification based on physical features?

options.text: DNA analysis is always wrong
Unrelated organisms can evolve similar physical features due to similar environments (convergent evolution), making them appear related when they are not
Physical features are always more reliable than DNA for classification
DNA does not contain information about physical features

questions.explanation: Convergent evolution causes unrelated organisms to develop similar features in response to similar environments (e.g., dolphins and sharks both have streamlined bodies but are not closely related). Physical classification might group them together incorrectly. DNA analysis reveals their true evolutionary relationships, as it is not affected by convergent evolution. This is why molecular evidence has reclassified many organisms.
